title: Transition coefficients on two nonvanishing opens are reciprocal on their intersection
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $s,t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ and let $U,V$ be opens with underlying sets $X_s,X_t$, respectively, where $X_a=\{x:a_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal M_x\}$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There exist $f\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ and $g\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ such that $U\cap V=D_U(f)$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] and $f|_{U\cap V}g|_{U\cap V}=1$ in $\Gamma(U\cap V,\mathcal O_X)$. Neither open need be affine; $X$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CY (lemma-s-open); Properties, proofs of Lemma 01PV (lemma-affine-cap-s-open) and Lemma 01PY

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] to $s$ and $t$. On $U$ and $V$ their multiplication maps from the structure sheaf are isomorphisms. The inverse maps applied to the other section give the unique coefficients $f,g$ with $t|_U=f s|_U$ and $s|_V=g t|_V$.

On U, convert the unique-coefficient conclusion for s into IsFreeGenerator of its restriction. Reuse stalk_generator_bijective from Sheaf.Paper.NonvanishingSectionTrivializes (accessed with a proof-only import all) to obtain a stalk basis at x in U. The basis spans the stalk, so Submodule.mem_smul_span_singleton and injectivity identify membership of a times the basis in maximalIdeal times the stalk with membership of a in maximalIdeal. Apply this to t_x=f_x s_x using germ_smul and germ_res_apply. IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal and Scheme.mem_basicOpen from [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] identify x in V with x in D_U(f). Outside U, both U intersect V and D_U(f) have no points by Scheme.basicOpen_le. This proves the equality without affine subopens or prime ideals, using the predicate [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

Restrict t|U=f s|U and s|V=g t|V to W=U intersect V. Naturality of scalar multiplication and composition of restrictions give s|W=g|W f|W s|W. Rewrite scalar composition as multiplication, commute f|W and g|W, and apply uniqueness of the coefficient of s|W from [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], comparing with its coefficient 1. This gives f|W g|W=1. The proof also works on the empty open, without a nonzero-ring hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Modules, Lemma 01CY; Properties, proofs of 01PV and 01PY; P2 proves the coefficient comparison directly with the stalk basis and Scheme.mem_basicOpen, without the affine prime-ideal lemma.

mathlib_searches.query: Two global sections of an invertible sheaf trivialize it on their nonvanishing opens and their transition functions multiply to one on the intersection
mathlib_searches.results: LeanSearch returned Internal Server Error; no absence conclusion drawn.

Scheme.mem_basicOpen identifies membership with invertibility of the germ of a function; basicOpen_le and basicOpen_pow also returned. None identifies nonvanishing of a module section with the basic open of its coefficient.

No hits in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry. Source basicOpen_coeff_eq uses Hom.zeroLocus instead of this module-section locus. Existing nonvanishing_section_trivializes provides unique coefficients but does not state their nonvanishing comparison.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nonvanishing_transition_functions {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (s t : M.val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) (U V : X.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X) = nonvanishingLocus M s) (hV : (V : Set X) = nonvanishingLocus M t) : ∃ (f : Γ(X, U)) (g : Γ(X, V)), U ⊓ V = X.basicOpen f ∧ (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op) f * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op) g = 1
